## Two weapons on your back, and a draw animation you pick by watching it

`back` maps 38 weapons. A rifle and a shotgun have always collided there — one of them simply
did not exist as far as anyone could see. This release draws both, and while we were in that
code the holster animation finally got the one thing it never had: someone looking at it.

49 commits. Multi-Weapon is **off by default**: turn it on and nothing else about your server
changes.

### Added: more than one weapon per body slot

The slots are body positions, not weapon families, so two long guns were never a rare case —
it was the ordinary load, and the second weapon was invisible. Dashboard → Core →
**Multi-Weapon**, `Max Per Slot` 1-4.

- **Distinct weapons get their own lane.** Copies of the same model share one prop: two
  identical rifles side by side read as a rendering fault, and every report that asked for this
  described *different* weapons. A distinct weapon always outranks another variant of one
  already shown — knowing *what* someone carries matters more than which accessory is on it.
- **The position is the switch.** A lane is an ordinary position: the 3D editor places it,
  per-job overrides apply to it, it persists. No lane position for a slot means no second
  weapon drawn there, which is also why nothing can end up stacked on top of itself.
- **Lane 1 never moves.** With the feature off you get exactly what you had before — not
  something similar, the same thing.
- The second rifle ships **placed**, tuned separately for male and female characters.

### Added: length classes

One tuned position has to hold a slot that runs from a sawn-off to a heavy sniper, so a short
weapon floats and a long one runs through the shoulder. A class (`compact` / `standard` /
`long`) is a **shift** applied on top of the position — not a second position — so it does not
multiply with the lanes. Shipped at zero: the mechanism is there, the tuning is yours.

### Added: the gesture picker — pick a draw animation by watching it

Dashboard → Placement → **Draw Style** → **Live Picker**. The panel steps aside, a camera
frames your character, and every holster animation in the game plays on it at the press of a
button. Keep the one that reads, per body slot, per direction.

A gesture cannot be judged from its name: `weapons@holster_2h / unholster` and
`reaction@intimidation@1h / intro` are equally plausible strings, and one of them is a man
threatening someone — which is what the pistol slot has been using since 1.0.

- **The clip and its duration are one decision.** Every slot has been playing a *fragment* of a
  longer animation — 19% of it for the pistol, 28% for the rifle — because the duration was
  tuned years ago against a different clip. Keeping a gesture now measures it and stores the
  length with it, so it plays whole.
- **Per-job draw styles.** Police draw one way, everyone else another. A style changes the
  gesture and never the timing, so no job draws faster than another.
- `/mbt_animaudit` on debug builds measures every animation against your game build: which
  exist, how long each runs, and which of your slots are cutting theirs short.

### Added: the editor tells the truth

- **Try a position against any weapon in the slot** before committing to it, instead of tuning
  against one model and hoping.
- **The slot's other lanes are drawn while you place one**, wearing the weapon you are looking
  at — the case that clips is two long guns, and it was the only one you could not see.
- Length-class shifts are tuned in the editor, on the same sliders.

### Added: the dashboard

- **Hidden by Job from the panel** — the per-job, per-slot rule that stops officers carrying two
  pistols now lives in the dashboard instead of `config.lua`.
- **Brand accent colour.** One colour, set by you, on every prompt and HUD your players see —
  with our own colour picker rather than the operating system's. It is your server's colour for
  its players; this panel keeps its own green.
- **Reorganised into seven categories** with a navigable index down the right side, and an
  Environment block that finally shows which framework, inventory and persistence the bridges
  actually resolved to.

### Changed

- **The tactical sling strap is now drawn for everyone**, not just for you. A strap across the
  chest exists to be seen by other people; it was local-player-only by an oversight. No network
  entity and no new event — every client draws it from what it already knows.
- **The suppressor glow sits on the suppressor.** The muzzle bone stays at the barrel's mouth
  while a suppressor bolts further forward, so the heat used to glow at its base. Applied only
  where a suppressor is actually fitted.
- Draw Style moved to the **Placement** page, with the other in-world editors.
- **Hidden by Job** no longer opens with a red button that throws away every rule; it sits at
  the foot of the card, next to the sentence explaining what it discards.

### Fixed

Four desyncs, **three of them older than this release**:

- **A player could stay invisible for an entire session.** If a client missed its own scope
  event, nobody ever saw its weapons — and because the failure is asymmetric, the symptom
  appeared to move between players depending on who you asked.
- **Entering a vehicle left a ghost weapon on your body** for everyone else, whenever you had
  both a pistol and a rifle slung.
- **Orphan props on leaving scope** — only what happened to be in one registry was cleaned up.
- **Emptying a slot did not trigger a re-read.** The guard checked the item's *name*, but an
  emptied slot arrives as `false`, so the one case that most needed the refresh never got it.

And, from the last day of work:

- **Drawing one of two slung weapons took both off your body** until the next inventory sync
  put the other back. The equip path cleared the whole *slot*, which was right while a slot
  held one weapon and wrong from the moment it could hold two.
- **Drawing while the prop was not on show recorded nothing at all** — during the half-second a
  prop takes to spawn, or while the weapon was concealed or hidden for your job. Putting it
  away then never brought it back.
- **The `ox_inventory` patch now updates when it changes.** Its marker was a number somebody had
  to remember to raise, and the first change that needed it did not get it, so servers kept
  running the old fragment and the Police draw style put the weapon away with the wrong
  animation. It is a hash of the patch itself now, and the patched file records which release
  wrote it.
- **`Hidden by Job` showed no jobs** on some servers while the same list rendered correctly
  elsewhere in the panel.
- **A style removed from `default.lua` could make your config permanently unsavable.** Settings
  pointing at a style that no longer exists are dropped instead of rejected.
- The position editor's **Reset All** no longer gets undone by the next ordinary save.
- Switching gender in the editor **moves the preview**, so you are no longer tuning the female
  position against the male pose.

### Note for server owners

**Restart the server after updating, not just the resource.** The `ox_inventory` patch changed,
so it is rewritten on start and `ox_inventory` has to recompile it.

**Multi-Weapon is off by default.** Nothing changes until you turn it on, and when you do, the
first weapon in every slot stays exactly where it is.

**Not tested this release:** the `qb-inventory` code path. The changes above are shared with
`ox_inventory` and were verified there. If you run qb-inventory and something looks wrong,
please open an issue — it will be fixed quickly.

### Install

Download `mbt_malisling.zip` below and drop it in your resources folder. Existing 2.0.x installs
upgrade in place — dashboard settings, placed racks, trunk contents and saved positions are all
kept.
